concerns.text: Task T013 lists dependency on T012.6 (`stream_nlcd_tiles.py`), but T012.6 is defined AFTER T013 in the task list. T013 cannot depend on a task that appears later in the execution flow. T012.6 must precede T013 to ensure the streaming logic is available for the merge operation.

Task T012.5 depends on T011 and T011.1 (EBD download), but the task description states it loads `ebd_train.csv` OR `ebd_train_fallback.parquet`. The dependency logic implies T011.1 must run if T011 fails, but T011.1 is marked [P] (parallel) alongside T011. If T011 runs successfully, T011.1 is redundant work. The ordering should reflect that T011.1 is a conditional fallback or T012.5 must explicitly handle the race condition of which file exists, rather than listing both as hard dependencies for a parallel block.

Task T019a and T019b are split parts of `models/train.py`. T019b depends on T019a. However, T019a is marked [P] (parallel-safe). A task that is part of a sequential split (Part A -> Part B) cannot be parallel-safe with its own successor. The [P] tag on T019a is incorrect as it implies it can run independently of T019b's completion, which violates the producer-consumer flow within the same file.

Task T020a and T020b are split parts of `models/evaluate.py`. T020b depends on T019 (training), but T020a also depends on T019. The dependency chain shows T020a and T020b as separate tasks, but T020b (Permutation Test) logically requires the metrics from T020a (Balanced Accuracy) to compare against the null distribution? Or does it run independently? If T020b needs the 'observed accuracy' from T020a to calculate the p-value, then T020b must depend on T020a. Currently, both depend only on T019, creating a potential race condition where T020b runs before T020a generates the observed metric.

Task T008a has a broken URL in the description: `https://ebird.org/api/checkpoint/v2/guilds` or a fallback CSV from the eBird GitHub releases (`). The closing parenthesis is missing, and the fallback URL is empty. This makes the task description ambiguous regarding the fallback source, which is critical for the dependency chain if the primary API fails.
